what_traders_are_doing: JULY 17 POST-CLOSE — V-RECOVERY FROM INTRADAY SUPPORT BREACH DEFINES THE SESSION. (1) THE KEY TECHNICAL EVENT — BTC's intraday low of $62,523 at 13:00 UTC breached the 200-week SMA support zone ($63,181) by $657. The fact that the CLOSE was at $64,115 (well above $63,181) is the single most important data point: the level was TESTED and HELD. In Wyckoff technical analysis, this pattern — where a support zone is briefly violated intraday and then reclaimed aggressively on the same session — is called a 'spring' or 'shakeout.' It typically signals that weak hands have been washed out and stronger buyers have taken control at the support level. (2) THE US MARKET RESPONSE — US institutional buyers showed up at the open (13:00 UTC / 9 AM ET) and bought the $62,523 dip immediately. By 17:00 UTC, BTC had reclaimed $64,000 on the highest-volume candle of the US session (236 BTC at 17:00 UTC = +$450 from $63,603 to $64,054). The pattern: US traders saw the dip, read the ETF flow data (+$79.15M on July 16 released today), and bought. (3) KIMI K3 CONTEXT — Moonshot's Kimi K3 is the most significant near-term AI competition threat since DeepSeek's January 2025 moment. Unlike DeepSeek (reasoning efficiency at low cost), Kimi K3 targets raw capability (2.8T parameters, 1M context, GPT-5.6-level performance). The 'open-weight' release July 27 will allow unrestricted fine-tuning and deployment — eliminating the API revenue stream that Anthropic, OpenAI, and others rely on. This is a structural AI-demand headwind: if models of this caliber are available for free, the case for spending $100B+ on GPU clusters weakens. For BTC, the Kimi K3 effect is second-order: AI speculation has driven some BTC correlation with AI names; Kimi K3 hurts AI valuations, which creates mild crypto risk-off. But BTC's flat close despite the global chip selloff (TSMC –7%, SMH –4%, VIX +12.2%) suggests the correlation is weak at current BTC price levels. (4) IRAN ESCALATION — Day 6 is different from Days 1–5: US is now targeting Iranian power plants and water infrastructure, and Iran is hitting US bases in Bahrain. The escalation pattern suggests Hormuz closure risk is rising. If Hormuz closes (even briefly), oil spike → global inflation surge → BTC risk-off. This tail risk has not been priced; it remains the single largest exogenous BTC headwind. (5) THE STOP IS THE LINE — $63,181 (200-week SMA zone floor) remains the stop condition. Today's test STRENGTHENED the case for the stop (buyers confirmed at this level). Next session: if BTC opens above $64,115 and holds, the V-recovery is confirmed. If it opens below and retests $63,181, that's the third visit to the zone in two weeks — still not a stop trigger unless it CLOSES below.

## Technical analysis (BTC — July 17, 2026, 22:00 UTC)

**Reference close:** $64,115.34 (20:00 UTC 1h candle close, Crypto.com BTC_USDT, TIER 1 verified). Down –$2.70 / –0.004% from July 16 reference of $64,118.04 — ESSENTIALLY FLAT. Session range: $62,523.13 (13:00 UTC low) – $64,392.98 (18:00 UTC high). Live price at 21:46 UTC: $64,097.28.

**Trend:** INTACT AT THE LINE — SPRING REVERSAL CONFIRMED ON CLOSE. The 200-week SMA / 50-DMA confluence zone ($63,181–$63,358) — the stop-loss reference for this framework — was tested intraday with the low hitting $62,523 (a $657 breach below $63,181). The reference close at $64,115 defended the zone by $934. This is the most important single-session technical event of the current framework: the support was found, tested, and held. The long-term trend read: BTC remains in a broad consolidation phase well below the 200-day MA (~$82,000, reflecting the 2025 peak); but within this consolidation, the 200-week SMA zone at $63,181 is the defining support and it held today.

**Momentum:** The three-day sequence since the July 15 monthly high:
- July 15: +0.61% (consolidation)
- July 16: –1.31% (Iran Day 5 + TSMC capex)
- July 17: –0.004% (FLAT; Kimi K3 + Iran Day 6; US buy-the-dip)

Momentum is stabilizing. The three-day decline from $64,971 (July 15 reference) to $64,115 (today) represents a –1.3% retracement of the July 14 CPI rally (+3.81%). The critical momentum signal: the US session produced the heaviest 8-hour volume block of the week (1,271 BTC) as prices recovered from the low — this is accumulation, not distribution.

**Pattern — V-Recovery (Spring Reversal):**
The session pattern: $64,118 open → $62,523 low (17 hours of selling) → $64,115 close (7 hours of recovery). The asymmetry (17h down, 7h up) is characteristic of a 'spring' in Wyckoff methodology: selling exhaustion at a key level followed by a rapid buying response. The spring is most powerful when it occurs at a well-defined support zone (here: the 200-week SMA at $63,181), which is the case.
